sources.note: Does not mention Tamki at all (Sokoro group represented only by Sokoro, from Marba 1990 SIL wordlist).

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2012. Classification and description of the Chadic languages of the Guera (East Chadic B). SIL Electronic Working Papers 2012-004. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Tamki stress (no prosody section for any language). Sec. 3 (printed p. 13): 'Tamki, Kujarge, and the nearly-extinct Mabire have only been documented in short wordlists and have otherwise never been studied (Dakouli et al. 1996..)'; sec. 4.2 excludes Tamki from the vowel survey because only wordlists exist; Appendix A p. 45 gives a Tamki consonant chart from 'SIL Chad wordlists'; Appendix B lists ~25 Tamki items, a few tone-marked (búsé, pìʔí, ɔ́ssɔ̀), none stress-marked.
Nothing; sole reference is Dakouli, Maass & Toomey 1996 (SIL ms.).

sources.citation: Martin 1999. Preliminary analysis of Sokoro (SIL Chad unpublished ms; treats Tamki as a dialect of Sokoro), cited in Lovestrand 2012.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Closest existing phonological analysis within the Saba-Sokoro-Tamki cluster by a fieldworker who regarded Tamki as a Sokoro dialect; if it has a prosody section it would be the nearest proxy statement (but it describes Sokoro, soko1263, not Tamki).

sources.note: Published description of the sister language Sokoro; may contain phonological preliminaries (tone/accent) for the cluster; not a Tamki source, proxy only.

sources.citation: Dakouli, Padeu, Antje Maass & David Toomey. 1996. Rapid appraisal of the Saba language of the Guera, Chad. N'Djamena: Association SIL. Manuscript (includes the 1995 Temki/Tamki 160-item survey wordlist; Glottolog ref 54391 'Dakouli 1995 Temki 160 survey word list').

sources.note: The only primary Tamki data known to exist; the wordlist transcription might carry stress or tone marks, and the report is the basis of every later mention of Tamki. Unpublished SIL Chad manuscript; would have to be requested from SIL Chad / SIL Language & Culture Archives.
